html:
SMTO-SCH-0019 — This schedule needs a future run time

GUID: 046c67d9-c5d1-435d-a56f-dafa82eaae22
Slug: schedule-next-run-invalid
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • A running schedule must have a next run time that is still ahead. This one has no next time, or its one-time date has already passed, so the change was not saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Schedules, select Edit on this schedule, and choose a date and time later than now. A one-time schedule whose time has passed has nothing left to run.
  2. Check that Time zone is the one you mean before you save. A time that looks later in your zone can already be past in a different zone.
  3. After saving the new time, select Resume if the schedule is paused. A paused one-time schedule with a past date needs a new date before it can be resumed.

What success looks like

  • The schedule's card shows a future date under Next run and no warning.

If it still fails

  • Select New schedule and enter the timing from scratch, or select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Schedule validation rejected an active schedule with no usable next_run_at, or a one-shot schedule whose next_run_at is missing or not in the future.

What this means

  • Active schedule validation finds no usable next occurrence, or an activated/edited one-shot next_run_at is absent or not future. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Active schedule validation finds no usable next occurrence, or an activated/edited one-shot next_run_at is absent or not future.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect effective status/type, next_run_at and current UTC time after applying the proposed edit.

How to fix it

  • normalized_event_update (and the Manager create path in schedule_manager.create_with_defaults) require an active schedule to have a next_run_at, and an active one-shot to have one later than now (UTC). Supply a future next_run_at in the schedule's timezone, or correct the calendar recurrence, before activating; keep the schedule paused until then.
  • Provide a valid future next occurrence or correct the calendar recurrence before activating.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Activation retains a valid intended future trigger or recurrence-derived occurrence.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
